keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Two 100 km discs, one on the Dhar Tichitt coordinates and one on Oualata (264 land cells, about 67,000 km2), for the "Tichitt-Oualata region"; the page gives about 500 settlements and compounds of 20-40 m, regional centres of 80 ha, no area. The page also says the cliffs "were inhabited by pastoralists and farmers between 4000 BP and 2300 BP", which is 2050-350 BCE.

ledger.note: 2600 BCE: the Pre-Tichitt pastoralists occupy the cliffs of Dhar Tichitt, Mauritania. "Pre-Tichitt (Phase I, Akreijit): 2600 to 1900 BCE."
1900 BCE: the Early Tichitt phase. "Early Tichitt (Phase II and III, Khimiya and Goungou): 1900 to 1600 BCE"; millet domestication newly dated "around 1900 to 1700 BCE".
1600 BCE: the Classic Tichitt phase of the massive stone compounds. "Classic Tichitt (Phases IV-VI, N'Khall, Naghez, and Chebka): 1600 to 1000 BCE."
1000 BCE: the Late Tichitt phase. "Late Tichitt (Phases VII and VIII, Arriane and Akjineir): 1000 to 400 BCE", a "Period of intense aridification and demographic decline".

ledger.note: 400 BCE: Tichitt is abandoned in the aridification. "Late Tichitt ... 1000 to 400 BCE"; the settlements "inhabited ... between 2000 BCE and 300 BCE"; the page gives no successor, so the land passes to nobody.

certainty.note: A cliff-top settlement landscape; no border is recorded.

sources.note: Chronology: Pre-Tichitt 2600-1900 BCE, Early 1900-1600, Classic 1600-1000, Late 1000-400; 500 settlements; Mauritania; 4000-2300 BP.

notes: Tichitt Tradition, Mauritania (the brief asked for "Tichitt precursors where dated"; the page dates the Pre-Tichitt phase from 2600 BCE, after the 3400 BCE horizon, so the whole sequence is drawn). The page gives two ranges: the phase chronology 2600-400 BCE (used) and "between 2000 BCE and 300 BCE" / "4000 BP and 2300 BP". Munson hypothesized pastoralists "around 4500 BP" (2550 BCE). No Cliopatria polity is near. Dhar Tichitt and Tichitt are not in the gazetteer; Oualata and a coordinate disc are used.
